:::{#def-positive-negative-parts}
#### Positive part of a function

Let $(S, \salg, \measure)$ be a [measure space](#def-measure-space),
and let $f : S \to \reals$ be [measurable](#def-measurable-function).
The **positive part** of $f$ is the non-negative function

$$
f^{+}(s) \eqdef \max\cb{f(s), 0}.
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-negative-part}
#### Negative part of a function

For $f$ as in @def-positive-negative-parts,
the **negative part** of $f$ is the non-negative function

$$
f^{-}(s) \eqdef \max\cb{-f(s), 0}.
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-positive-negative-parts}
#### A function in terms of its positive and negative parts

With the positive part (@def-positive-negative-parts) and negative part (@def-negative-part),
$f = f^{+} - f^{-}$ and $\abs{f} = f^{+} + f^{-}$.
($f^{+}$, $f^{-}$, and $\abs{f}$ are measurable when $f$ is
[@billingsley1995probability, Theorem 13.3].)

:::
